business_problem: City of Hope needed to let prospective patients begin intake after hours and on weekends without adding staff or taking patient-access representatives away from phone support. Existing chat in some markets depended on daytime call-center availability, while patient access teams needed to avoid repeatedly collecting information patients had already provided.
solution_summary: City of Hope added an Agentforce chat intake experience to its existing Salesforce-supported patient intake process. The agent collects preliminary demographic and registration information and gives patients instructions for tasks such as uploading an insurance card, allowing them to begin when they are available rather than waiting for staffed phone or chat hours. Patient responses are saved as records in the Salesforce environment, and a conversation summary gives patient access representatives context for the next step. Marketing Cloud uses appointment creation or new patient information in Salesforce to trigger automated journeys, welcome kits and follow-up communications; Tableau supports operational analysis. Staff refine prompts and language, and cases needing additional help are routed to the contact center or followed up by representatives. The source describes this intake and handoff flow, but not the underlying AI model or data-storage implementation.

Appointments or new patient information in Salesforce trigger Marketing Cloud journeys, and Tableau is used to analyze operations. Interactions needing additional support are handed to the contact center or patient access team.

business_outcome: Agentforce lets patients begin the intake process outside staffed hours, reduces reliance on manual chat interactions and helps representatives continue the conversation with information patients have already shared. Salesforce's reported results include 43% of Agentforce-scheduled appointments occurring outside business hours and 3.5% of total appointments being initiated through Agentforce in a four-week period.
